approval_source.question_set: The six questions P01_T05_FAULT_ALERTS_2026-11-09 left unset

follow_up.question_set: Four follow-ups from the first CI run of the decisions (PR #128)

decisions.question: Which alert (host and condition) each in-scope fault must raise
decisions.rule: The partition raises the sentry's consensus_halt; host loss the sentry's heartbeat alert (monitoring_down, the alerting service's 180 s rule); the sentry rebuild the sentry's monitoring_down; the validator host the sentry's consensus_halt and the validator's monitoring_down.

decisions.question: Host loss: whether its outage must cross an alert threshold, and how
decisions.selected: Keep the 180 s heartbeat rule; lengthen the CI host-loss down time past 180 s
decisions.rule: The CI host-loss drill holds the sentry off for more than 180 s so its heartbeat alert must fire. The 10-minute recovery target is still measured from the power-on.

decisions.question: Network partition: whether a 90 s cut must reliably raise the 60 s consensus halt alert
decisions.selected: Lengthen the partition to at least 150 s
decisions.rule: The partition lasts at least 150 s, rather than accepting a miss with the once-a-minute monitor.

decisions.question: When the alert must fire and resolve relative to the fault's window
decisions.selected: Fire before recovery, resolve after recovery
decisions.rule: Each alert must fire before the fault's recovery and resolve after its recovery.

decisions.question: How many repetitions the KPI needs, and whether CI evidence can count for it on the public page
decisions.selected: The fault campaign's count for each fault; CI counts toward the tools phase only
decisions.rule: Each fault needs the same number of repetitions as the fault campaign uses for it. CI evidence counts toward the tools phase only; only real staging-host runs count on the public page.

decisions.question: Whether reinstalling a host's monitor settings is part of the sentry rebuild and validator host recovery procedures
decisions.rule: Redoing the monitor settings is part of the rebuild and replacement procedures; the procedure documents say so.

decisions.question: The CI sentry rebuild (45 s) and validator host (55 s) end before any alert threshold
decisions.selected: Hold them down past 180 s, as for host loss
decisions.rule: In CI the sentry-rebuild and validator-host drills are held down past 180 s, as long as host loss is held off, so their alerts must fire.

decisions.question: Host loss has no repetition count in the fault campaign
decisions.selected: The same count as the partition
decisions.rule: Host loss needs the same number of repetitions as the partition.

decisions.question: An alert seen resolving by the once-a-minute monitor before the reader records recovery
decisions.rule: An alert that resolves up to one monitor period (60 s) before the recorded recovery still counts as resolving after recovery.

decisions.question: The real-host alert pipeline
decisions.rule: The real-host alert pipeline is deferred to staging. CI evidence counts toward the tools phase only.

supersedes.part: Its unset list: each item is decided here.

does_not_authorize: any run on a real host
